content:
Overview

Purpose built student accommodation continues to outperform much of the wider real estate market. Strong domestic and international student growth, limited new supply and rising pressure on local rental markets are together creating a clear opportunity for long-income investment. This Insight summarises the essential demand drivers shaping the sector today and the implications for developers, lenders and institutional capital.


A Growing Student Population

The UK’s student base has expanded steadily over the past decade. Applications from UK school leavers continue to rise, participation in higher education remains structurally high and the demographic swell in the eighteen-year-old population is adding further momentum. International demand remains resilient, helping reinforce student numbers in key university cities. These trends have combined to create a larger and more stable pool of renters for modern, well managed accommodation.


Persistent Supply Constraints

Against this backdrop of rising demand, delivery of new PBSA has struggled to keep pace. Planning delays, construction cost inflation, land scarcity and competing residential priorities mean new stock is arriving slowly. Graduate cities such as Manchester, Bristol, Leeds and Birmingham, alongside major university clusters, face pronounced shortfalls. Older HMO stock is also leaving the sector due to energy standards, licensing requirements and landlord exit, adding pressure to already tight markets.


Rising Rents and Affordability Challenges

The imbalance between demand and supply has fed directly into rent inflation. PBSA rents have risen consistently since 2021, with several cities experiencing notable year-on-year increases. Many students are now being priced out of traditional rental markets and are either pushed towards more expensive university or PBSA options or choosing to remain at home. For investors, this environment strengthens occupancy resilience but also underlines the need to deliver schemes that strike a balance between quality and affordability.


Where Demand Is Strongest

Demand is most robust in cities anchored by high-performing universities and a balanced domestic and international intake. Russell Group locations remain core, but several mid-tier cities are also seeing intense pressure due to limited private rental supply and strong student recruitment. In these markets, professionally managed PBSA with strong amenities, good transport links and credible operating partners typically achieves near-stabilised occupancy each academic year.

Institutional Capital Continues to Scale


PBSA has cemented its position as a mature institutional asset class. UK investment volumes have grown, driven by forward funding, site acquisitions and large platform transactions. Investors are attracted by the reliability of student demand, the inflation-protected nature of income and the ability to reposition existing assets to meet ESG requirements. The key challenge is managing development risk and ensuring income durability in an environment of rising costs and changing regulatory expectations.


Opportunities for Investors and Developers

The sector continues to offer prospects for disciplined capital. Opportunities include forward funding in high-demand cities, refinancing stabilised schemes, upgrading older stock to improve operational efficiency and leveraging risk transfer solutions to strengthen cashflow certainty. Structures that protect rental income from adverse events can help reduce funding costs, improve leverage and enhance asset valuations, making long-income PBSA more compelling to lenders and investors.
